events.title: Battle of Crécy
events.description: English forces under Edward III met a larger French army in northern France. English and Welsh longbowmen cut down wave after wave of charging French knights and crossbowmen.
events.significance: The battle showed that disciplined archers could defeat armored cavalry. It was a turning point in medieval warfare and an early triumph for England in the Hundred Years' War.

events.title: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
events.description: France's National Constituent Assembly approved this foundational charter in the first weeks of the Revolution. It declared that all men are born free and equal in rights.
events.significance: The declaration shaped modern ideas of liberty, equality and the rule of law. It influenced later human rights documents around the world.

events.title: Krakatoa Begins Its Cataclysmic Eruption
events.description: The volcano in the Sunda Strait of Indonesia entered its violent final phase, with powerful explosions and ash columns. It culminated the next morning in one of the loudest and deadliest eruptions in recorded history.
events.significance: The eruption and the tsunamis it caused killed tens of thousands of people. Its ash also affected global weather and produced vivid sunsets for months.

events.title: 19th Amendment Certified
events.description: The United States officially certified the 19th Amendment to the Constitution, which barred denying the vote on the basis of sex. The certification followed ratification by the required number of states.
events.significance: Millions of American women gained the right to vote. The date is now commemorated each year as Women's Equality Day.

events.title: Cardinal Albino Luciani Elected Pope John Paul I
events.description: The cardinals chose the Patriarch of Venice as pope after a short conclave. He became the first pope to take a double name, and was known for his warm smile.
events.significance: His reign lasted only 33 days, and the Church held another conclave that year. That conclave elected John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope in centuries.
